questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

The Manager warned his team members (1)/ that if they persist in their (2)/ obstructionist attitude they would be punished. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: 2**

**'Persist' must be replaced by 'persisted'. Since the main clause is in the form 'would be punished' (would+infinitive), the conditional clause must have simple past (persisted). **

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Both taciturn and ______, Daniel seldom spoke and never spent money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'miserly'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• In this context, "**miserly**" best fits the blank in the sentence.
 
• The sentence indicates two characteristics of Daniel: he is quiet, as indicated by "taciturn", and he does not spend money.
 
• "**Miserly**" means being careful with how money is spent, often excessively so, which fits the description.
 
• So, the completed sentence reads: "Both taciturn and miserly, Daniel seldom spoke and never spent money."
 
• Let's look briefly at the other options:
 
 
• "**Wary**" means being careful or cautious about possible dangers or problems. It doesn't directly relate to not spending money.
 
• "**Cheap**" is sometimes used colloquially to mean a reluctance to spend money, but it is a less formal term and can also have negative connotations implying poor quality.
 
• "**Discreet**" means careful and prudent in one's speech or actions, especially to keep something confidential or to avoid embarrassment. It doesn't relate to spending habits.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

He was too _____ to make a statement before the Boss.​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3** i.e. **timid.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence suggests a degree of reluctance or fear in making a statement before the Boss.
 
• The word **"timid" **(डरपोक) means showing a lack of courage or confidence, which fits this context.
 
• The words **"shy," "tired,"** and **"coward"** partially fit but do not convey the same exact meaning. "Shy" may be close, but "timid" is more precise in the context of reluctance to speak up.
 
• Understanding the meaning of **"timid"** aids in clearly identifying why he was reluctant to speak before the Boss.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is **timid**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *He was too **timid__** to make a statement before the Boss.​*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Shy (**संकोची) means being reserved or having feelings of nervousness.
 
• **Tired (**थका हुआ) means in need of rest or sleep.
 
• **Coward (**कायर) means lacking courage to face danger or pain.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Reiterate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Repeat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"reiterate"** means to say something again or a number of times, typically for emphasis or clarity. (दोहराना)

 
 
• **Example:** The teacher had to reiterate the instructions to ensure everyone understood.
 
 
 
• **"Repeat"** refers to saying or doing something again. (फिर से करना)
 
 
• **Example:** Please repeat your question so that everyone can hear it.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Repeat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Abuse** (दुरुपयोग): Use (something) to bad effect or for a bad purpose.

 
 
• **Example:** He abused his power to exploit the workers.
 
 
 
• **Pretend** (बहाना करना): Speak and act so as to make it appear that something is the case when in fact it is not.
 
 
• **Example:** She pretended that she was feeling alright.
 
 
 
• **Detest** (घृणा करना): Dislike intensely.
 
 
• **Example:** She detests bad manners.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Adamant
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: Flexible**

'Adamant' refers to a person who is rigid on his decisions or actions. 'Rigid', 'fixed' and 'unshakable' are synonymous to 'adamant'. 'Flexible' can be used to describe someone who isn't very steadfast or firm. Thus, 'flexible' is the antonym of 'adamant'.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".

Father (would have been appreciated) your efforts if you had informed him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __would have appreciated__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The subordinate clause of the sentence is in the past perfect tense (subject + had + third form verb). To maintain the uniformity of the sentence the main clause will have the structure as "would have + past participle". Hence, the main clause will take the verb phrase as:- "would have appreciated".
 
• The given sentence is a third conditional sentence.
 
• A third conditional sentence is used to imagine a different past that did not happen.
 
• Some Examples:-__

 
• If I had been present, I should have enjoyed it a lot. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dac933c583d88d7fbb203b5b7a234cec3fd685de718148e906afdace8b6dc680.png] 
 
• If I had been present, I would have enjoyed it a lot. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f6f8e13711bfe65ee7caffc30a728d21e8ef2dcdd208f14056c5bdc3aa26945.png] 

__The correct sentence is__- *Father __**would have appreciated**__ your efforts if you had informed him.*

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Find the incorrectly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Leakeage**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The incorrectly spelt word is '**Leakeage**'. The correct spelling is "Leakage". 
 
• Leakage: Leakage refers to the unintentional or accidental escape or loss of a substance, typically a liquid or gas, through a crack, hole, or other opening. It implies a leakage of a substance from its intended containment.
 
 
• Example: There was a leakage in the water pipe, causing a small pool to form on the floor.
 
 
 
• Let us look at the meaning of other words:
 
• **Literary**: Literary refers to anything related to literature or written works, particularly those of high artistic or intellectual value. It encompasses genres such as novels, poetry, plays, and essays.
 
 
• **Example**: The literary world celebrated the release of the author's highly anticipated novel.
 
 
 
• **Laudable**: Laudable describes something deserving praise, admiration, or commendation due to its excellent qualities, actions, or achievements. It implies that the subject is praiseworthy and worthy of recognition.
 
 
• **Example**: The organization's laudable efforts to support underprivileged children earned them widespread appreciation.
 
 
 
• **Loafer**: A loafer refers to a person who is idle, lazy, or avoids work or exertion. It can also refer to a type of comfortable slip-on shoe, typically made of leather, without laces or buckles.
 
 
• **Example**: He was labeled as a loafer because he constantly avoided his responsibilities and rarely made an effort to contribute to the team's work.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Find the incorrectly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Anasthetic**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The incorrectly spelt word is "Anasthetic". Its correct spelling is '**anesthetic**'.
 
• **Anesthetic**: Anesthetic (also spelled anaesthetic) refers to a substance or medication used to induce anesthesia, a state of temporary loss of sensation or consciousness. It is commonly used during medical procedures to numb pain or induce sedation.
 
 
• **Example**: The dentist administered a local anesthetic before starting the tooth extraction to ensure a painless experience for the patient.
 
 
 
• Let us look at the meanings of other words:
 
• **Obliterate**: Obliterate means to completely destroy or erase something, leaving no trace or evidence behind. It implies the complete elimination or annihilation of an object, concept, or memory.
 
 
• **Example**: The powerful explosion obliterated the building, reducing it to rubble within seconds.
 
 
 
• **Concurrence**: Concurrence refers to the simultaneous occurrence or agreement of multiple events, opinions, or actions. It suggests a state of alignment or harmony between different elements.
 
 
• **Example**: The concurrence of favorable weather conditions and a well-prepared team resulted in a successful outdoor event.
 
 
 
• **Blithesome**: Blithesome describes someone or something that is cheerful, lighthearted, and full of joy. It conveys a sense of happiness and carefree spirit.
 
 
• **Example**: The children played in the park, their laughter filling the air, creating a blithesome atmosphere.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: But the scenario has quite changed nowadays by allocating a special budget of funds for security.

Q: In the last ten years, budget towards the development of military forces is higher when compared to others.

R: India earlier days gave more importance to the development of industry and less importance to other departments.

S: This is because of the frightening increase in terrorism all around the world especially emerging after the 9/11 terror attack in the U.S.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: RPSQ**

Statement R talks about the past, mentioning how more importance was given to development of industry as compared to the other departments. This must logically be the first sentence. The second sentence must be P. This is because P states a contrast to the earlier situation while staying in line with the topic at hand. Statement S states the reason behind this contrast. Thus, it must be the third sentence. Statement Q must follow statement S as it furthers the point and shows the consequences of the ever-increasing terrorism all around the world.

**Note:**

RP is a pair because R says that before India's budget gave importance to industrialisation, but now scenario has changed.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

One should keep one's word.

options.text: One's word has to be kept
One's word should be kept by us

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: A word should be kept.**

Option 3 has replaced 'should' by 'has'. This cannot be the answer. Option 4 has changed the subject to 'us' and therefore cannot be the answer. Option 2 uses the wrong tense for the verb. The verb must in the past participle form. Thus, the correct answer is option 1 which fulfils all the rules. (The subject has been omitted)

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in the Indirect/Direct speech.**

The old man said, "Thanks I shall never forget this kindness, Ankit."

options.text: The old man applauded Ankit for his kindness and he shall never forget Ankit
The old man thanked Ankit and assured him that he would never forget his kindness
Ankit was being thanked by the old man for his kindness towards an old man
The old man said thank you to Ankit for his kindness.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The old man thanked Ankit and assured him that he would never forget his kindness**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The given sentence is in the direct mode of narration. The reporting verb is in the simple past tense, there will be a change in tense.

When we convert this particular sentence from the direct to the indirect mode of narration, we have to make the following changes:

 
• Since the reporting verb is in the simple past tense, all the verbs in the reported speech will undergo a backshift of tense:
 
• **'shall' **is changed into **'would'**
 
• Simple present 'thank' is changed into simple past 'thanked**'**
 
• 'this' is changed to 'that'
 
• **'I' **is changed into **'he'**

​Following these steps here we find that the correct sentence is Option 2 which is the correct answer.

questions.question: National integration means _____ all the people of the nation into a single whole.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: combining**

To integrate something means to bring things together or to combine them. Thus, the blank must be filled by 'combining'. 'Segregating' means to separate things. 'Residing' means that the power of something is vested in someone else . 'Complying' is to act in accordance with someone else's wishes

questions.question: It is a _____ that binds together
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: sentiment**

The blank is preceded by the article 'a'. Out of the four options, only 'sentiment' can follow the singular article 'a'. The rest are plural.

questions.question: all people in one _____ bond no matter what their religion, caste, language or history
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: common**

The sentence is meant to put forward the idea that despite the differences in religion, caste, language and history, the people are brought together in one common bond. Thus, the blank must be filled with 'common'.

questions.question: It is a _____ cementing force whereby all kinds of people
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: strong**

The phrase 'cementing force' is indicative of strength and adhesiveness. Thus, the correct answer is 'strong'.

questions.question: live _____ peacefully and can identify themselves as a part and parcel of a nation.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: together**

The idea of the sentence is to make the people live in harmony with one another. Logically, 'together' fits the sentence in the best manner.
